page.layout: Running head at top centre. Above the text: one block of italic verse (first poem), full width. Below it: a rule, then a centred heading "IN PHILOPATRVM." with a verse of two stanzas. Then a centred heading "In eundem." with a further verse. A page number at the lower right. No marginal notes.

p.i: Vt mortem simulat! scelesta, prodi, Pro tot criminibus datura pœnas. Age, istum iugulo tuo cruento Mucronem excipe, & istum, & istum, & istum Vide vt palpitat, vt cruore largo Aras polluat hæc profana sacras! At vos Pierides, bonaque Musæ, Nunc gaudete: Iacet fera interempta, Iacet sacrilega illa, quæ solebat Sacros Pieridum vorare seruos. Hanc vero tunicam, has dico, Camœnæ, Vobis exuuias, vt hinc trophæum Parnasso in medio locetis, & sit Hæc inscriptio: De fera interempta Beza dat spolia hæc optima Musis.
DAmnabis (fateor) nostros, Philopatre, libel- Et tibi non lectum despicietur opus. Quid tum? si nostros, carpas, Philopatre, libellos: Debebunt tanto nostra placere magis.

SIue Palatina Philopatrus inambulet aula, Et fatuo incessu marmor vtrúmque terat: Siue fames illum locupletum quarere mensas, Et procul è Sacra iussit abire domo: Seu ieiunus eat, seu pleno ventre vacillet,

page.notes: Running head partly cut off at the top edge; read as "THEOD. BEZÆ". The page number "5" at the lower right is small and uncertain. Several line ends at the right edge are cut off by the scan edge (e.g. "libel-", "Iacet", "inambulet aula,"); the words are read as far as visible. The first line of the Latin verse "Vt mortem" is in italic with mixed long s forms, transcribed as plain s. The heading "IN PHILOPATRVM." is a title above a poem and set at level 2.
